captures.notes: The shortened lower arcade selects a denser attempt with eleven connected buildings and substantially more overhead route cover than the rejected seed-3 candidate. Roof and plank materials remain consistent.
The opposite overview shows a compact stepped block instead of scattered buildings. Exterior ground is visible around its edge but not through a central urban shaft.
The section verifies staggered narrow/tall building proportions, complete roofs, and supported galleries; no room shell is open at the top or intersecting a neighbor.
The seven-to-eight-cell ground market branch turns twice within nearby inhabited mass, eliminating the former long exposed road through this seed.
The hostile reverse view is terminated by construction and a route turn, with occupied and public surfaces above it rather than a view through to the far grass.
The cross-route passage is externally navigable but compressed by facades, stairs, retained structure, and upper floors. The visible horizon belongs to the perimeter exit.

The previously over-broad opaque upper court is now divided by six separated one-fine-cell lightwells with complete guards. It still serves multiple nearby entrances and remains part of the public graph.
The occupied link is roofed and joined to inhabited endpoints. Dense adjacent mass limits the full silhouette from this hostile angle but does not hide a missing roof or open seam.
The underside confirms a true occupied overpass above exterior circulation and naturally dark undersides without the former dark walk-top glitch.
The complete roofline contains no roofless room or outcropping. Pitched runs and gables close their measured envelopes without clipping adjacent houses.
The final network view shows six bounded non-adjacent lightwells breaking up the upper district, a one-component route, and a maze geometry distinct from the other three seeds.
